title: Oklahoma State 16, Oklahoma 13: The November 24, 2001 Bedlam Upset
question: What happened when Oklahoma lost to Oklahoma State 16-13 on November 24, 2001?
answer: Three-win Oklahoma State upset No. 4 Oklahoma 16-13 in Norman on November 24, 2001, with a late Josh Fields touchdown pass to Rashaun Woods. The loss ended OU's 19-game home winning streak and its shot at the Big 12 title game.
summary: Oklahoma State stunned No. 4 Oklahoma 16-13 on Nov. 24, 2001, ending the Sooners' 19-game home winning streak and their Big 12 title-game hopes.
body: On November 24, 2001, No. 4 Oklahoma came into the Bedlam game at 10-1, with its only loss at Nebraska. Oklahoma State was 3-7 overall and 1-6 in the Big 12. The Sooners also carried a 19-game winning streak at home into Norman.

Quentin Griffin gave Oklahoma a 7-0 lead with an 8-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, and the Sooners led 13-6 in the fourth after a short field goal. Oklahoma State answered with a 52-yard field goal to make it 13-9, then kept the pressure on the OU offense.

The deciding play came late. Quarterback Josh Fields hit receiver Rashaun Woods in the left corner of the end zone from the Oklahoma 14-yard line, with Woods outleaping cornerback Derrick Strait. The extra point made it 16-13.

The result ended the home streak and knocked Oklahoma out of the Big 12 Championship Game picture, which Colorado won over Texas. Bob Stoops' team bounced back by beating Arkansas 10-3 in the 2002 Cotton Bowl Classic and finished No. 6 in the final AP poll.
For Oklahoma State fans it remains one of the great Bedlam upsets, and for Sooner fans it is a reminder that the rivalry can overturn any record.
